title: THE SAME HAND, THE SAME HEAD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"He is to present the bull at the entrance to the tent of meeting before the LORD. He is to lay his hand on its head and slaughter it there before the LORD."'" - Lev 4:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The high priest of Israel — the most spiritually privileged man alive, the one who wore God's name on his forehead — stands at the same entrance as everyone else, lays his hand on a head, and kills the animal himself.

No shortcut. No assistant. No private ceremony. The same gesture the poorest Israelite made.

There is something deeply levelling about this. Spiritual position does not create a separate category of access to God. Aaron approached exactly as the farmer approached: by substitution, by blood, by God's appointed way.

The New Testament states the principle without qualification. All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God (Rom 3:23) — and the "all" includes the pastor, the missionary, the person who has walked with God for fifty years. There is no advanced route.

This protects us from two errors. It stops us idolising spiritual leaders as though they operate on a higher plane. And it stops us disqualifying ourselves as though our ordinary faith were second-rate.

One entrance. One kind of sacrifice. One way in. Jesus said, "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me" (Jn 14:6). Not one path for the mature and another for the struggling. One.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I imagine mature Christians have some access to God that I lack?
2. Am I still coming to God by grace, or have I drifted into relying on my track record?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that there is one way to You and it is open to me today. Keep me from pride and from self-disqualification alike. Amen.
